$comment: Line-count ceilings for the modules where Otto feature code accumulates fastest.
These are RATCHETS, not targets. A ceiling may only ever be LOWERED. When an extraction
wave moves code out of one of these files, lower its ceiling in the same commit so the
space cannot be reclaimed by the next feature.
Raising a ceiling is not a normal action. If a change genuinely needs one raised, that is a
signal the feature wants its own module instead. See docs/architecture.md for the domain
structure Paseo uses (server/session/<domain>/, protocol/src/<domain>.ts) and prefer adding
a sibling module over growing one of these.
Set 2026-08-19 at each file's then-current size.
Re-baselined 2026-08-23 at each file's then-current size. The 2026-08-19 numbers went red
within days -- 18 of the 21 files were over by the 0.8.14 release, several by hundreds of
lines -- so the lint job failed on this check every run and stopped being read as a signal.
A ceiling nobody can get green gates nothing. These numbers restore the gate against FUTURE
growth; they are not an endorsement of the current sizes. Draining them is tracked in Otto
Knowledge under 'Oversized-module inventory (the standing refactor backlog)', and the rule
above is unchanged: the way to pass this check is a sibling module, not a bigger number.
